evidence.quote: In 2003 Jefferson Township was granted Ohio Scenic Byway status by ODOT

evidence.claim: The township actively manages and protects the corridor’s historic character.
evidence.quote: the township actively manages and protects the historic character of the 15 miles of the Jefferson Township Scenic Byways corridor.

evidence.claim: Many of the older barns and homes date from the early 1800s.
evidence.quote: older barns and homes, many dating from the early 1800s

evidence.claim: Gahanna and Columbus have annexed most of the township’s western and southern portions, leaving small township islands within the cities.
evidence.quote: Most of these islands are surrounded by either Gahanna or Columbus, cities that have annexed most of the western and southern parts of the township.

evidence.claim: Gahanna borders the township on the west, offering a starting point beside Big Walnut Creek.
evidence.quote: Gahanna was founded along the Big Walnut Creek in 1849

evidence.claim: Gahanna borders the township on the west
evidence.quote: Jefferson Township: east

evidence.claim: East of Gahanna, the township’s landscape includes stream corridors, hills and ravines associated with Rocky Fork, Blacklick and Swisher creeks.
evidence.quote: stream corridors, hills, ravines, and slopes, much of it associated with the waterways, tributaries, and floodplain that Jefferson Township is in from Rocky Fork, Blacklick, and Swisher Creeks

evidence.claim: East of Gahanna
evidence.quote: Jefferson Township: east

evidence.claim: Rocky Fork tributaries also cross New Albany, the township’s northwestern neighbor.
evidence.quote: The tributaries of Rocky Fork, Rose Run and Sugar Run, flow northeast to southwest throughout the city.

evidence.claim: the township’s northwestern neighbor
evidence.quote: New Albany – northwest

evidence.claim: Two villages once faced each other across Granville Street beside Big Walnut Creek.
evidence.quote: Located directly across Granville Street from Gahanna and also along the banks of the Big Walnut Creek, Bridgeport was founded in 1853 by Jesse Baughman

evidence.claim: John Clark founded Gahanna in 1849 on land his father had bought in 1814.
evidence.quote: Gahanna was founded along the Big Walnut Creek in 1849 by John Clark of Ross County from 800 acres (320 ha) of land that his father, Joseph Clark, had purchased from Governor Worthington in 1814.

evidence.claim: Jesse Baughman founded neighboring Bridgeport four years later.
evidence.quote: Bridgeport was founded in 1853 by Jesse Baughman

evidence.claim: The rivals eventually merged, keeping Gahanna’s name because Ohio already had another Bridgeport.
evidence.quote: The two villages eventually put aside their differences and merged into one. They adopted the name Gahanna as there was already another village in Ohio called Bridgeport.

evidence.claim: In 1881, residents petitioned for incorporation, and the joined village held its first mayoral election that year.
evidence.quote: In March 1881, 55 citizens of Gahanna petitioned Franklin County to incorporate the village. The incorporation was granted in June and was recorded on August 8, 1881. The now-incorporated village then held its first mayoral election

evidence.claim: The creek remains central to the city’s geography, joined by Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run.
evidence.quote: Big Walnut Creek has a significant impact on the geography of Gahanna associated with its tributaries Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run.

evidence.claim: A creekside redevelopment and park extension begun in 2004 added public spaces, residences and places of business to Olde Gahanna.
evidence.quote: In October 2004, Gahanna's new Creekside Gahanna redevelopment and park extension project began, making way for everything from public spaces and restaurants to residences and office space.

evidence.claim: Blacklick’s name came from its creek after its first name proved unavailable.
evidence.quote: It was originally named Smithville, but there was an existing town by that name so it was renamed to Blacklick after the nearby creek.

evidence.claim: William A. Smith established the community in 1852 as Smithville.
evidence.quote: The community was established by William A. Smith in 1852.  It was originally named Smithville

evidence.claim: Historian W. Edson Richmond thought the creek had been named for landowner H. G. Black, but John F. Mansfield’s 1806 Ohio map already labels it Blacklick Creek; Black was born in 1817.
evidence.quote: It was thought by historian W. Edson Richmond that Blacklick Creek derived its name from local landowner H. G. Black.  However, Richmond references John F. Mansfield's Map of the State of Ohio from 1806 which labels Blacklick Creek, while Henry George Black was not born until 1817.

evidence.claim: The stream flows through the community in southern Jefferson Township, which is also home to the township’s active Jefferson Cemetery.
evidence.quote: Blacklick Creek flows through Blacklick.

evidence.claim: the community in southern Jefferson Township
evidence.quote: Blacklick is a small unincorporated community in southern Jefferson Township

evidence.claim: home to the township’s active Jefferson Cemetery
evidence.quote: Blacklick is the site of Jefferson Cemetery, an active cemetery operated by Jefferson Township.

evidence.claim: Its post office once stood within the community, but moved just south of it on Reynoldsburg-New Albany Road.
evidence.quote: The Blacklick Post Office (zip code 43004) used to be within the community, but has moved just south of the community on Reynoldsburg-New Albany Road.

evidence.claim: Rocky Fork begins in the New Albany area, where Rose Run and Sugar Run cross the city from northeast to southwest.
evidence.quote: New Albany is situated in the headwaters of the Rocky Fork, a tributary of Big Walnut Creek. The tributaries of Rocky Fork, Rose Run and Sugar Run, flow northeast to southwest throughout the city.

evidence.claim: Nobel Landon and William Yantis founded the town in 1837, dividing land into lots 50 feet wide and 100 feet long.
evidence.quote: The land of New Albany was founded in the center of Plain Township in 1837 by Nobel Landon and William Yantis. The land was split into lots measuring 50 ft (15 m) by 100 ft (30 m) and sold to new settlers.

evidence.claim: The 1980 census counted only 414 residents.
evidence.quote: As late as 1980, the census only listed 414 residents in the village.

evidence.claim: Rapid growth began in the 1990s, partly through Les Wexner’s investment; changes to State Route 161 and its I-270 connection brought freeway access.
evidence.quote: Rapid growth in New Albany began in the 1990s, partly due to the expansion of the Les Wexner clothing empire and Wexner's construction of his mansion

evidence.claim: changes to State Route 161 and its I-270 connection brought freeway access
evidence.quote: State Route 161 and access to 161 from I-270 was reconfigured around this time, allowing freeway access into and out of town.

evidence.claim: Three roads divide the city center: Dublin-Granville, Johnstown Road and New Albany-Reynoldsburg Road.
evidence.quote: Three main roads intersect the city center: Dublin-Granville, U.S. Route 62/Johnstown Road, and New Albany-Reynoldsburg/Ohio Route 605/New Albany-Condit.

evidence.claim: Blacklick Creek crosses the city’s eastern end.
evidence.quote: Blacklick Creek flows through the eastern end of the city.
